AccountDeleteRequest.description: Explicit confirmation, so a stray click cannot destroy an account.
AccountDeleteRequest.title: AccountDeleteRequest

AccountDeleteResponse.description:
Result of a tombstone deletion.

``r2_delete_failures`` is deliberately part of the success body rather than
being swallowed: reporting "deleted" while a resume object is still live in
object storage would be a false claim (D-07).

r2_delete_failures.description: Object keys that could not be removed from R2. Empty is the happy path.
r2_delete_failures.title: R2 Delete Failures

AccountDeleteResponse.title: AccountDeleteResponse

AccountExportResponse.description:
Every identified data class held for the authenticated user.

``profile`` is the raw ``users.profile_data`` blob, so it is typed as an open
object: its key set is genuinely per-user until Phase 2 decomposes it.

assessment_answers.description: The subject's own answers. Keyed by intent rather than after the table they come from, so an internal schema name does not become part of a public contract.
assessment_answers.title: Assessment Answers

profile.description: Raw profile_data blob. Open-ended until Phase 2 (P0-1).
profile.title: Profile

AccountExportResponse.title: AccountExportResponse

AgentChatRequest.description:
A chat turn. The response is Server-Sent Events, not JSON.

The server prepends its own system message carrying RAG context assembled
from the profile, the company network, and the user's resume text -- so the
client must not send a system message of its own expecting it to be honoured.

messages.description: Full conversation history; must be non-empty.
messages.title: Messages

AgentChatRequest.title: AgentChatRequest

AssessmentFormResponse.description:
The person-side items, ordered for this respondent.

The payload carries ``blocks``, not ``dimensions``. The client renders it
verbatim: it must not sort, group, re-shuffle, or reorder options. Ordering
is server-authoritative because two independent PRNGs in two languages
diverging is silent, and a divergence corrupts a resumed session's ordering
rather than raising (D-04).
AssessmentFormResponse.title: AssessmentFormResponse

AssessmentSubmitResponse.description:
Deliberately does not carry the six dimension scores.

The documented threat to this instrument is aspirational answering by a user
self-profiling for matching. Handing back the six numbers gives a retaking
respondent a gradient to optimise against -- it teaches the
item-to-dimension mapping that the shuffle and the interleave exist to hide.
AssessmentSubmitResponse.title: AssessmentSubmitResponse

CompanyDetailResponse.description:
One company's full stored research profile.

``id`` is the integer primary key and appears in the URL, so this endpoint
enumerates: an authenticated caller can walk the ids and read the whole
network. Part 4.2 replaces it with a UUID ``public_id``.

``profile`` is the serialised ``CompanyProfile`` from
:mod:`packages.ml.culture` -- open here because its optional sections vary
by how much research a company has had.
CompanyDetailResponse.title: CompanyDetailResponse

CultureMatchEntry.description:
One scored company.

``top_matching_dimensions`` and ``top_mismatching_dimensions`` are the two
highest- and two lowest-scoring dimensions, and ``fit_summary`` is the
sentence built from them.
CultureMatchEntry.title: CultureMatchEntry

CultureMatchesQuery.description:
Query parameters for the culture-match list.

No cursor: this endpoint returns two fixed-size slices rather than a page,
and Part 5.2 is where it becomes a properly paginated ``/me/matches``.

limit.description: Companies per list. Clamped to 1-50; a non-integer is a 400.
limit.title: Limit

CultureMatchesQuery.title: CultureMatchesQuery

CultureMatchesResponse.description:
Best and worst culture fits for the authenticated user.

When at most ``2 * limit`` companies score, the two lists partition the
whole set at its midpoint rather than each taking a slice off the end -- so
a company never appears in both.
CultureMatchesResponse.title: CultureMatchesResponse

DashboardResponse.description:
Job-seeker dashboard summary.

``recentActivity`` and ``recommendations`` are static placeholders in the
current implementation; the three counts are live.
DashboardResponse.title: DashboardResponse

EarlyAccessRequest.description:
Landing-page interest form.

Not persisted -- the submission exists only as an email to
info@solverah.com. A delivery failure loses the lead, which is why this is
the one intake endpoint that returns 500 rather than swallowing the error.
EarlyAccessRequest.title: EarlyAccessRequest

ExportedAccount.description: Identity fields of the exporting user.
ExportedAccount.title: ExportedAccount

ExportedIntakeSubmission.description: One pre-launch intake submission matched to the account's email.

resume_filename.description: Basename of the stored object, not the R2 key. The key is an internal locator and exporting it would hand out a storage path.
resume_filename.title: Resume Filename

ExportedIntakeSubmission.title: ExportedIntakeSubmission

ExportedLegacyQuiz.description: The pre-assessment-table quiz payloads held on ``UserIntake``.
ExportedLegacyQuiz.title: ExportedLegacyQuiz

FocusTypeSubmitRequest.description: Five scene payloads, scored deterministically -- no LLM on this path.

scene_3.description: Time split across deep_solo, planning, social, breaks, exploring.
scene_3.title: Scene 3

FocusTypeSubmitRequest.title: FocusTypeSubmitRequest

IntakeCreateAccountRequest.description: Register a new account from a finished submission.
IntakeCreateAccountRequest.title: IntakeCreateAccountRequest

IntakeFinalizeRequest.description:
Step 2 of 2. The server HEADs the object before recording the row.

Without that check a client could skip the upload entirely and still create
a submission pointing at a key that holds nothing.

linkedin_url.description: Must be an https://linkedin.com URL if present.
linkedin_url.title: Linkedin Url

IntakeFinalizeRequest.title: IntakeFinalizeRequest

IntakeLinkAccountRequest.description:
Submit the intake form while already signed in.

Same body as finalize minus the email, which comes from the JWT -- recording
the body's email instead would let a signed-in user file a submission under
someone else's address.

email.description: Ignored. The submission is recorded against the JWT identity.
email.title: Email

linkedin_url.description: Must be an https://linkedin.com URL if present.
linkedin_url.title: Linkedin Url

IntakeLinkAccountRequest.title: IntakeLinkAccountRequest

mime.description: Must be PDF, DOC, or DOCX.
mime.title: Mime

size.description: Exact byte count; bound into the signature.
size.title: Size

IntakePresignResponse.description:
Step 1 of 2. The browser PUTs the file to ``upload_url``.

``submission_id`` is a v4 UUID and is the only thing protecting an anonymous
submission -- there is no account to authorise against, so the object key is
deliberately unguessable.

upload_url.description: Presigned PUT URL, valid for 10 minutes.
upload_url.title: Upload Url

IntakePresignResponse.title: IntakePresignResponse

IntakeSaveToAccountRequest.description:
Persist an anonymous Work Pulse Lite-Lite session onto the account.

Called right after login when sessionStorage still holds data from the
``/start`` flow.
IntakeSaveToAccountRequest.title: IntakeSaveToAccountRequest

IntakeSignInRequest.description:
Attach a submission to an existing account by signing in.

The email must match the one on the submission, so a submission cannot be
attached to an unrelated account by guessing its id.
IntakeSignInRequest.title: IntakeSignInRequest

IntakeSignInResponse.description: Same envelope as a login: JWT in an HttpOnly cookie, CSRF token in the body.
IntakeSignInResponse.title: IntakeSignInResponse

LegacyError.description:
The pre-Phase-1 error body: ``{"error": "..."}``.

Handlers return this from their own explicit failure branches, and Phase 1a
keeps every one of them byte-for-byte.  It coexists with
:class:`ProblemDetailResponse`, which is what the Phase 0 error handlers
produce for anything a handler did not catch itself.

The two shapes are why ``src/utils/apiError.ts`` reads both.  Phase 1b
collapses them by moving handlers onto ``solverah.errors.ApiError``.
LegacyError.title: LegacyError

LoginResponse.description:
Successful login. The JWT arrives as an HttpOnly cookie, not in the body.

``csrfToken`` is the double-submit half of the scheme: the client stores it
in memory and echoes it as ``X-CSRF-TOKEN`` on every state-changing request.
Appendix B calls this scheme correct and preserved verbatim.
LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse

LogoutResponse.description:
Always ``{"message": "logout successful"}``.

The cookie is cleared with ``Set-Cookie`` on this response.  Note that the
JWT itself remains valid until it expires -- clearing the cookie ends the
browser session but cannot revoke the token, which is exactly what Part 5.3's
database-backed refresh tokens are for.
LogoutResponse.title: LogoutResponse

ManagerMatchResult.description: Deterministic scoring merged with the LLM-generated narrative.
ManagerMatchResult.title: ManagerMatchResult

OkResponse.description: The bare acknowledgement several handlers return.
OkResponse.title: OkResponse

PasswordResetVerifyResponse.description:
Passwordless sign-in result.

Same envelope as :class:`LoginResponse` but with the summary user: this path
does not return ``profileData`` or the assessment-completion flags, and the
difference is preserved rather than harmonised.
PasswordResetVerifyResponse.title: PasswordResetVerifyResponse

PathPreferencesRequest.description:
The three career-search preferences.

All three are required and validated against closed sets: the path scorer
branches on them, so an unrecognised value would silently change ranking
rather than fail.
PathPreferencesRequest.title: PathPreferencesRequest

PathSuggestion.description: One suggested O*NET occupation with its narrative.

profile_dimensions.description: Which parts of the profile drove the match.
profile_dimensions.title: Profile Dimensions

PathSuggestion.title: PathSuggestion

PathSuggestionsResponse.description:
Scored and narrated career paths, cached per user.

A 400 with ``career_status_not_set`` means the profile is missing a field
the scorer requires, and the client should prompt for it. A 500 means O*NET
or the narrator failed, and the client should retry.
PathSuggestionsResponse.title: PathSuggestionsResponse

ProblemDetailError.description: One field-level entry inside a problem document's ``errors`` array.
ProblemDetailError.title: ProblemDetailError

ProblemDetailResponse.description:
RFC 9457 problem document, as emitted by ``solverah.errors``.

Served with ``Content-Type: application/problem+json``.  This is the body
for anything the handler did not answer itself: an unhandled exception, a
404 on an unknown path, a 405, a 413 over ``MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH``, a 429 from
the limiter.

request_id.description: Correlation id, echoed as X-Request-Id. Quote it in bug reports.
request_id.title: Request Id

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.
status.title: Status

title.description: Short, stable summary of the problem type.
title.title: Title

ProblemDetailResponse.title: ProblemDetailResponse

ProfileReadResponse.description:
``GET /profile`` -- the entire user document.

Note ``csrfToken``: the read doubles as the client's way of recovering a
CSRF token after a page reload, since the token is held in memory and the
JWT cookie is HttpOnly. That is the reason this endpoint is on the app-boot
path at all, and Part 5.2's ``GET /auth/session`` is what replaces it.

csrfToken.description: Echo as X-CSRF-TOKEN on state-changing methods.
csrfToken.title: Csrftoken

profileData.description: Raw profile_data blob. Open-ended until Phase 2 (P0-1).
profileData.title: Profiledata

ProfileReadResponse.title: ProfileReadResponse

ProfileSaveRequest.description:
``POST /profile``.

Keys inside ``profileData`` are filtered server-side by
``validators.clean_profile_data`` -- an unknown key is dropped, not
rejected, so the model is open here to match.

profileData.description: Partial profile. Merged over the stored blob; unknown keys are stripped.
profileData.title: Profiledata

ProfileSaveRequest.title: ProfileSaveRequest

QuizInsightsGuestResponse.description:
Anonymous preview. Nothing is persisted.

Note the key: this returns ``overallSummary`` where the authenticated
endpoint returns ``overallInsight``. Both are read by the frontend, so the
inconsistency is preserved rather than fixed here.
QuizInsightsGuestResponse.title: QuizInsightsGuestResponse

QuizInsightsRequest.description:
Quizzes to generate insights for.

A quiz with no key, no title, or no answered items is discarded before the
model is called; if that leaves nothing, the request is a 400.
QuizInsightsRequest.title: QuizInsightsRequest

overallInsight.description: Cross-quiz synthesis, when the model returns one.
overallInsight.title: Overallinsight

key.description: Echoed verbatim in the matching insight.
key.title: Key

RecommendationsResponse.description:
Job recommendations.

Currently always empty: the ML pipeline that produced these was replaced by
the AI agent and the Groq-backed replacement is not wired up. Both the GET
and the POST are stubs that return this shape, which is why the frontend
renders an empty state rather than an error.
RecommendationsResponse.title: RecommendationsResponse

RegisterRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /register``.

``terms_accepted`` must be boolean ``true`` -- the handler compares with
``is True``, so a truthy string is rejected. That is deliberate: consent
evidence should not be satisfiable by accident (GAP-01/GAP-05).

terms_accepted.description: Must be literal true. Recorded in profile_data as evidence of assent.
terms_accepted.title: Terms Accepted

terms_version.description: Version assented to; stored as "unversioned" when absent.
terms_version.title: Terms Version

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

object_key.description: Key from the presign step. Must be under profile/{your-user-id}/.
object_key.title: Object Key

ResumeFinalizeResponse.description:
Step 2. Parsing runs inline, which is P0-6.

Part 5.2 turns this into a 202 with a job handle once Phase 3's queue
exists; the response shape below is the synchronous one it replaces.
ResumeFinalizeResponse.title: ResumeFinalizeResponse

mime.description: Must be PDF, DOC, or DOCX.
mime.title: Mime

size.description: Exact byte count; bound into the signature.
size.title: Size

ResumePresignResponse.description:
Step 1 of the two-step upload. The browser PUTs to ``upload_url``.

``size`` from the request is signed into the URL as ``ContentLength``, so a
client that declares 1 KB and uploads a gigabyte is rejected by R2 rather
than trusted by us.

upload_url.description: Presigned PUT URL, valid for 10 minutes.
upload_url.title: Upload Url

ResumePresignResponse.title: ResumePresignResponse

url.description: Presigned GET URL, valid for 10 minutes.
url.title: Url

SendEmailFailureResponse.description:
The 500 body when Resend rejects a send.

Carries ``detail`` on the resend path only, which is where the original
handler included it.
SendEmailFailureResponse.title: SendEmailFailureResponse

SessionUser.description:
The user object returned on a successful login.

``profileData`` is the entire ``users.profile_data`` blob.  Shipping the
whole user document on every session restore is the god-endpoint problem
Part 5.2 splits apart; it is documented here rather than quietly trimmed,
because trimming it would break the frontend that reads it.

profileData.description: Raw profile_data blob. Open-ended until Phase 2 (P0-1).
profileData.title: Profiledata

SessionUser.title: SessionUser

SkillProficiencyResponse.description: Confirming proficiencies also stops the rating modal re-prompting.
SkillProficiencyResponse.title: SkillProficiencyResponse

SummaryUser.description: The identity fields returned where no profile payload is wanted.
SummaryUser.title: SummaryUser

WorkPulseResult.description:
Work Pulse narrative result.

Persisted to ``user_intake.wpl_result`` and returned verbatim by
``GET /work-pulse/results``.
WorkPulseResult.title: WorkPulseResult

WpllResultResponse.description:
The teaser insight plus the titles of the sections still locked.

Two shapes can come back on a 200: the LLM-generated one below, and the
deterministic rules-engine fallback when the provider call fails. Both carry
``insight_text`` and ``locked_sections``, which is why the fallback is
invisible to the client -- and why it is safe here and nowhere else.
WpllResultResponse.title: WpllResultResponse

accessTokenCookie.description: HttpOnly JWT set by POST /api/v1/login. Not readable by JavaScript, so it is paired with the CSRF header below on every state-changing method.
accessTokenCookie.name: access_token_cookie

csrfHeader.description: Value of the csrf_access_token cookie, echoed by the client. Required on POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
csrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-TOKEN

info.description:
POST /work-pulse/submit - Generate and persist a Work Pulse narrative.

Validates the 12 WP answers, calls OpenAI with a structured prompt that
optionally incorporates earlier WPLL signals from the user's intake row,
then persists the answers and narrative to user_intake.
info.title: Solverah API

post.description:
POST /account/delete - erase personal data; keep de-identified research rows.

Body (JSON): {"confirm": "DELETE"} - explicit confirmation string so a
stray click or replayed request cannot destroy an account.
post.summary: Erase personal data, retaining de-identified assessment rows

get.description: GET /account/export - one JSON document of everything we hold.
get.summary: Export every identified data class held for the authenticated user

post.description: Responds with `text/event-stream`, not JSON: one `data: {"chunk": ...}` frame per token, then `data: {"done": true, "model": ...}`. A failure that happens mid-stream is delivered as a `data: {"error": ...}` frame on a 200, because the status line has already been sent.
post.summary: Stream a chat turn from the AI agent

get.description:
GET /assessment/form - the person-side items, ordered for this respondent.

The payload carries `blocks`, not `dimensions`. The client renders it
verbatim: it must not sort, group, re-shuffle, or reorder options. Ordering
is server-authoritative because two independent PRNGs in two languages
diverging is silent, and a divergence corrupts a resumed session's ordering
rather than raising.
get.summary: Fetch the person-side assessment items, ordered for this respondent

post.description:
POST /assessment/submit - score and persist a completed assessment.

The six dimension scores are NOT returned. The documented threat to this
instrument is aspirational answering by a user self-profiling for matching,
and handing back the six numbers gives a retaking respondent a gradient to
optimise against -- it teaches the item-to-dimension mapping that the
shuffle and the interleave exist to hide. Whatever the user is eventually
shown about their own profile should be designed against that pressure, not
fall out of the submit response by default.
post.summary: Score and persist a completed person-side assessment

get.description: GET /companies/<company_id> - Return a company's full profile.
get.summary: Fetch a company's full research profile

get.description:
GET /company-lens/matches - Score all companies against culture preferences.

Returns the best and worst fits. A user who completed Work Pulse before
culture_preferences was persisted gets it backfilled here, which is why a
GET can write.

parameters.description: Companies per list. Clamped to 1-50; a non-integer is a 400.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Rank companies by culture fit for the authenticated user

post.description:
POST /confirm-email - Verify the 6-digit OTP sent at registration.

Checks that the code matches, has not expired (default 15 min window), and
clears the token fields on success so the code cannot be reused.
post.summary: Verify the 6-digit code sent at registration

get.description:
GET /dashboard-data - Return summary stats for the job-seeker dashboard.

Computes profile completion percentage, job-match count, and application
count from live data. Also returns static placeholder recommendations and
recent activity until those features are fully wired up.
get.summary: Summary statistics for the job-seeker dashboard

post.description:
POST /early-access-request - Early-access interest form (no resume).

Accepts a lightweight JSON body from the landing-page modal and forwards the
details to info@solverah.com via Resend. Does not persist to the database.
post.summary: Register interest from the landing-page modal

post.description:
POST /focus-type/submit - Score and persist a FocusType result.

Accepts the 5 scene payloads, runs deterministic scoring, and persists the
archetype result to user.profile_data["focus_type_result"].
post.summary: Score and persist a FocusType result

post.description:
POST /intake/create-account - Register a new account from an intake submission.

Looks up the intake record by submission_id, validates the chosen password,
creates a User row with email_confirmed=False, and sends a verification
email. The intake record's status is updated to "account_created".
post.summary: Register a new account from an intake submission

post.description:
POST /intake/finalize - Commit an intake submission after resume upload.

Step 2 of 2. The client provides personal details and the object key from
the presign step. The server validates all fields, verifies the uploaded
object exists in R2 and matches the declared size and type, inserts the row,
and sends an internal notification email.
post.summary: Commit an intake submission after the resume upload

post.description:
POST /intake/link-account - Submit the intake form for an authenticated user.

Records the submission against the JWT identity, verifies the upload, then
merges the parsed resume into the user's profile.
post.summary: Submit the intake form as an already-authenticated user

post.description:
POST /intake/presign - Generate a presigned S3 PUT URL for resume upload.

Step 1 of 2 in the intake flow. The client sends the file's MIME type and
size; the server validates both, generates a UUID-based object key, and
returns a short-lived presigned PUT URL for direct browser-to-R2 upload.
post.summary: Presign an upload URL for an anonymous resume submission

post.description:
POST /intake/save-to-account - Persist anonymous WPLL session data to the account.

Called by the frontend immediately after login when sessionStorage contains
intake data from the /start flow. Creates the user_intake row on first call;
upserts on subsequent calls (preserves wpl_* fields if already set).
post.summary: Persist an anonymous quiz session onto the authenticated account

post.description:
POST /intake/sign-in - Sign in and attach an intake submission to an account.

Used when the user already has an account and returns through the intake
flow. After successful authentication, the intake's parsed profile data is
merged (intake values win on conflict) into the user's existing profile.
The intake status is updated to "account_linked".
post.summary: Sign in and attach an intake submission to an existing account

post.description: POST /intelligence/path-preferences - Save career search preferences.
post.summary: Save the user's career search preferences

get.description:
GET /intelligence/path-suggestions - Score and narrate career path suggestions.

Orchestrates path_scoring.score_paths and path_narrative.generate_narratives,
caching the result per user. The cache is invalidated when the user's
WorkPulse results, experience entries, or ManagerMatch results are updated.
get.summary: Score and narrate career path suggestions

post.description:
POST /login - Authenticate a user and issue a JWT cookie.

Validates credentials, enforces account lockout after MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS
consecutive failures, and requires email confirmation before granting
access. On success, sets an HttpOnly JWT cookie and returns the CSRF token
in the response body (so the frontend can attach it as X-CSRF-TOKEN on
mutating requests).
post.summary: Authenticate a user and issue a JWT cookie

post.description:
POST /logout - Clear the JWT cookie server-side.

Flask-JWT-Extended's unset_jwt_cookies removes the access-token cookie from
the response, effectively ending the session.
post.summary: Clear the JWT cookie

get.description: GET /manager-match/results - Retrieve the persisted ManagerMatch result.

post.description:
POST /manager-match/submit - Score and persist a ManagerMatch result.

Validates 15 forced-choice answers, runs deterministic scoring, calls OpenAI
to generate a personalised narrative, then persists the full result to
user.profile_data["manager_match_result"].
post.summary: Score and persist a ManagerMatch result

get.description:
GET|POST /profile - Read or update the authenticated user's profile.

GET returns the full profile including profileData and the current CSRF
token, and writes a `read` audit log entry (P0-3).

POST merges incoming profileData keys into the existing profile (unknown
keys are stripped by clean_profile_data). Quiz results are merged at the
sub-key level so existing quiz entries are preserved. Diffs against the
stored parser snapshot to record ResumeParseCorrection rows for any
experience/education/skills the user edits after a resume upload.
get.summary: Read or update the authenticated user's profile

post.description:
GET|POST /profile - Read or update the authenticated user's profile.

GET returns the full profile including profileData and the current CSRF
token, and writes a `read` audit log entry (P0-3).

POST merges incoming profileData keys into the existing profile (unknown
keys are stripped by clean_profile_data). Quiz results are merged at the
sub-key level so existing quiz entries are preserved. Diffs against the
stored parser snapshot to record ResumeParseCorrection rows for any
experience/education/skills the user edits after a resume upload.
post.summary: Read or update the authenticated user's profile

patch.description:
PATCH /profile/career-status - Directly set the user's career_status.

Lets the frontend set career status with a single targeted request rather
than a full profile save. Used by the career-status onboarding modal so the
user can pick a status without filling in experience entries.

get.description:
GET /profile/resume-url - Get a presigned download URL for the user's resume.

Generates a short-lived (10-minute) presigned GET URL for the resume stored
at the resumeKey in the user's profile, so the browser can download or
display the file without exposing permanent storage credentials.
get.summary: Presign a download URL for the stored resume

post.description:
POST /profile/resume/finalize - Parse the uploaded resume and update profile.

Verifies the object key belongs to the requesting user, downloads the
resume from R2, runs the rule-based parser, and merges the parsed fields
(experience, education, skills) into the user's profile. Also stores a
_parsedResumeSnapshot so subsequent edits can be diffed against the
parser's original output (see ResumeParseCorrection).
post.summary: Parse an uploaded resume into the profile

post.description:
POST /profile/resume/presign - Presign a PUT URL for authenticated resume upload.

Scopes the S3 object key to profile/{user_id}/{uuid}/resume.{ext} so that
one user cannot overwrite another's file. Step 1 of 2.
post.summary: Presign an upload URL for a new resume

patch.description:
PATCH /profile/skills/proficiency - Bulk-update skill proficiency ratings.

Accepts a list of { name, proficiency } objects and writes them into the
skill_levels dict in profile_data. Also sets skills_proficiency_confirmed
so the proficiency modal is not re-shown on the next Path Intelligence
visit.

post.description:
POST /quiz-insights - Generate and persist AI career insights.

Validates and normalizes the quiz answers, calls OpenAI with a structured
prompt, coerces the response to a canonical schema, and persists the
insights into profile_data.quizInsights.
post.summary: Generate and persist AI career insights

post.description:
POST /quiz-insights-guest - Generate AI insights for unauthenticated preview.

Same logic as /quiz-insights but requires no JWT. Hard-limited to 1 request
per day per IP to reduce OpenAI spend. Insights are NOT persisted to any
user profile.
post.summary: Generate AI career insights for an unauthenticated preview

get.description:
GET /recommendations - Return persisted job recommendations for the user.

The ML pipeline that generated these has been replaced by the AI agent.
Returns an empty list until a Groq-based recommendation flow is wired up.

post.description:
POST /recommendations - Trigger job recommendation generation.

Accepts a profilePipeline payload but is currently a no-op stub while the
Groq-based recommendation flow is being built.
post.summary: Trigger job recommendation generation

post.description:
POST /register - Create a new user account.

Creates the user with ``email_confirmed=False`` and sends a 6-digit OTP. The
user must confirm their email before they can log in. Profile data is
pre-seeded with a blank default profile appropriate for the given role.
post.summary: Create an account and send its verification code

post.description: POST /request-password-reset - Send a 6-digit OTP for passwordless login.
post.summary: Send a sign-in code to a confirmed account

post.description:
POST /resend-confirmation - Issue a fresh OTP for unconfirmed accounts.

Regenerates and re-sends the 6-digit verification code. Rate-limited to 5
per minute to prevent abuse.
post.summary: Issue a fresh verification code for an unconfirmed account

post.description:
POST /verify-password-reset - Validate OTP and issue a JWT.

Validates the 6-digit OTP, clears it on success, and issues a JWT cookie
plus CSRF token so the user is fully logged in without a password.
post.summary: Exchange a sign-in code for a session

post.description:
POST /work-pulse/lite-lite/result - LLM-powered insight for the WPLL teaser.

Anonymous endpoint - no auth required. Calls OpenAI to generate a
personalised 2-3 sentence insight from the 5 WPLL answers, then returns it
alongside the fixed set of locked section titles shown on the result screen.
Falls back silently to the rules-based engine if the LLM call fails or
returns a malformed response.
post.summary: Generate the anonymous Work Pulse Lite-Lite teaser insight

get.description:
GET /work-pulse/results - Retrieve persisted Work Pulse results.

Returns the stored narrative, emerging signals, and archetype from the
user's most recent Work Pulse submission. Used by the results page to
rehydrate state in fresh browser sessions where sessionStorage has been
cleared.
get.summary: Retrieve the stored Work Pulse result

post.description:
POST /work-pulse/submit - Generate and persist a Work Pulse narrative.

Validates the 12 WP answers, calls OpenAI with a structured prompt that
optionally incorporates earlier WPLL signals from the user's intake row,
then persists the answers and narrative to user_intake.
post.summary: Generate and persist a Work Pulse narrative
